conclusions: 1. ROBUST WIN (holds on all 3 tremor weight sets tested): tremor-branch phase-2 fine-tune 50 ep @ lr 1e-3 with batch 8, plus scaling the L2-normalised typing embedding by 0.3 in FusionModel.call. Tremor F1 +0.09 to +0.16, FMI/PD F1 -0.01 to -0.03. V0 (your current weights): C0 0.783/0.887/0.887 -> C17 0.942/0.860/0.860 (tremor/FMI/PD). T1: C6 0.807/0.916/0.897 -> C9 0.925/0.884/0.888 (5 reps). T1b: C15 0.781/0.852/0.850 -> C18 0.866/0.841/0.841.

2. The stronger tremor fine-tune is the key part: batch 8 alone does not help (C1, 1 rep: tremor 0.727). The fine-tune alone already gives tremor +0.10 on V0 (C5 0.883); the 0.3 typing scale adds the rest by weakening the typing->tremor shortcut (FMI-only subjects 4 and 13).

3. PRETRAINING: no robust gain. T1 (tremor without permute_segments) produced the best runs (C6, C9), but an identical re-run (T1b) did not reproduce them, so pretraining-seed variance is as large as the configuration effects. Typing augmentation (Y2) raised the linear probe by +0.10 AUC but did not improve downstream FMI (C3 = C0). T3/T5 had the best tremor probes but were worse downstream (C13, C14). The linear probe does not predict downstream performance. Recommendation: keep the current pretrained weights (V0); do not rerun pretraining.

4. Routing the tremor output to the tremor embedding only (ARCHITECTURE CHANGE; C10, C11, C16) fixes subjects 4 and 13 in every run but gives about the same tremor as the no-architecture-change recipe above, so it is not needed.

5. FMI/PD sit at 0.84-0.92 in every configuration, capped by typing-branch errors on subjects 1, 5, 15, 21 (wrong in nearly every run). Nothing tested robustly improves FMI: typing pretraining (Y2), typing downstream LP-FT (C12), and fusion-head variants all fail to.
6. Subject 19 (tremor) is a false negative in almost every configuration: a branch-level failure no fusion setting fixes.
7. Single-run F1 on 22 subjects moves by up to about +-0.05; compare configurations by the mean over reps (3-5 reps here).
